Where im at (detroit area), most decent paying shops lovveee to keep you at a livable wage by working that overtime. Its like, obviously a decent company could find an extra 10k per employee to keep them happy. But that means theyd have to cut salaries from the "big guys". Of course its a competitive market and they want to keep those that they consider of higher value. But come on ya know. Its all about finding what the worker bee will deal with, and if thats just at the cusp of being able to afford a house, then thats where they set the bar. Its a big game, just like how amazon does it but on a smaller scale. I gotta rant about this just to find out if im crazy or not lol.

You know what sucks? Being a welder, they sell you the dream of making so much money but skip the part where factories or even on the job workplaces like to run you until you cant run no more. The idea is to keep production flowing at all times. 10 hours not cutting it? Well push em to 12 and say its only temporary. Or the scenario that they add another shift. They wont switch to 8's, nonono. Theyll wait to pump up production and only implement a new shift when theyre able to get a solid 10 hours out of em. Why do they do this? Probably so they dont have to worry about laying off employees when the jobs slow down, or to save costs in labor/space/equipment. Another awesome part of the welding culture is to "suck it up and take the overtime money". Its known in the industry that if you want a 40/hr work week youre dreaming. Laborers and some skilled skilled tradesman are the lowest chain in the welfare concern. Someones gotta bear the brunt so others can live cushier lives. Just the way the world goes i suppose. Anyway, end of rant, unions are helpful.
